answer: Attention Ledger Expiry. Each identity must spend a minimum number of verified human-attention intervals inside a shared context window before its actions count, and unused capacity decays like a karst aquifer draining through limestone rather than pooling. The ledger records only time-on-task, so a farm must keep every puppet continuously engaged or watch its balance fall below the threshold where votes resolve, much as a river loses volume to seepage before reaching the sea. Idle identities also emit a slow signature, a plume of decay that flags over-provisioned operators.
